chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad narrated from Muʿāwiyah ibn Ḥukaym, from Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a woman sees blood at the beginning of her menstruation and the blood continues, she leaves the salat (prayer) for ten days, then she performs salat (prayer) for twenty days. If the blood continues with her after that, she leaves the salat (prayer) for three days and performs salat (prayer) for twenty-seven days.
Al-Ḥasan said, and Ibn Bukayr said: This is among those matters from which they find no escape.

key_terms.اَلدَّمَ: blood seen by the woman in the ruling described
key_terms.اَلصَّلَاةَ: the salat (prayer) that is suspended or resumed according to the ruling
key_terms.ثَلَاثَةَ أَيَّامٍ: three days during which salat (prayer) is later left
key_terms.سَبْعَةً وَعِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا: twenty-seven days during which salat (prayer) is then performed
key_terms.عَشَرَةَ أَيَّامٍ: ten days during which salat (prayer) is left initially
key_terms.عِشْرِينَ يَوْمًا: twenty days during which salat (prayer) is performed after the initial period

ai.seo_question: What should a woman do with salat (prayer) if bleeding continues from the beginning of her menstruation?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a woman whose bleeding continues from the onset of her hayd. It outlines how many days salat (prayer) is to be left and resumed in recurring cycles, indicating a practical jurisprudential framework for ongoing bleeding.
